title: 1986 contractor recommendation whether to launch STS-51L in unusually cold conditions

decision_cutoff.date_or_period: 27 January 1986, immediately before the final oral recommendation at approximately 11 p.m. Eastern Standard Time (UTC-05:00)
decision_cutoff.definition: Morton Thiokol management's choice whether to maintain engineering's no-launch recommendation or reverse it, before communicating its final oral recommendation when the teleconference resumes. Local Kennedy Space Center discussion during the separate Thiokol caucus is attributed locally; its receipt by the remote contractor managers is not established. The subsequent recommendation, fax and post-recommendation objections are excluded.

packets.masking_note: Audit packet; famous case is readily recognisable.
Mission, organisation, vehicle, exact dates, O-ring label and famous temperature values removed; evidence relationships and decision pressure retained.

expected_constitutional_constraints: When an irreversible high-consequence action faces material safety uncertainty, uncertainty must not be converted into evidence of safety.
The burden of justification should increase with foreseeable consequence and irreversibility.
A safer reversible alternative such as delay must be considered against schedule/customer pressure.
Engineering dissent and the initial no-launch recommendation must be communicated rather than disappearing through managerial aggregation.
Commercial/institutional pressure is not safety evidence.
Decision-makers should distinguish absence of conclusive proof of failure from evidence that the system is safe outside its experience base.

sources.citation: Presidential Commission on the Space Shuttle Challenger Accident, Chapter V: The Contributing Cause of the Accident
sources.use_note: Reconstructs launch decision process and Commission findings from testimony and documents.

sources.citation: A.J. McDonald, typed account of January 27 events, reproduced in Rogers Commission hearings
sources.use_note: Numbered note pp. 5 and 7 supply earlier dissent and the locally proposed delay; p. 9 discomfort follows the oral recommendation and remains reveal-only. Page 14 contains the February 13 addendum. The entire typed item is not certified as a contemporaneous verbatim transcript.
